summary: Batch B remains fail-closed. The additive v4 selector correctly keeps acceptance red and selects the additive Kimi WebBridge v3 audit for B4, but 86 required active-receipt provenance fields are unavailable, the only independent review predates and does not hash browser-v3, and no candidate, approval, or accepted manifest exists. The browser record discloses synthetic input, hidden-tab scheduler replacement, no student-data access, and session closure, but those operational assertions are not independently tool-attested and Village Guardian completion POSTs returned 400.

blocking_findings.title: Active role receipts cannot authenticate isolation, provenance, or append-only authority
blocking_findings.detail: The active v4 receipt gate reports 86 unavailable required provenance values across the eleven selected receipts. The v4 truth receipt has null prompt, actual context, spawn/session, ancestry, fork_turns, raw isolation proof, start/end events, final response, and commit fields. The browser-v3 receipt likewise has null provider spawn/session, ancestry, fork_turns, start/end events, final response, and commit. Git commits show one repository author identity, which cannot establish distinct role sessions. Git additions preserve prior files, but file addition and local SHA-256 values do not substitute for provider-attested fresh-context, fork_turns=none, or append-only event provenance required by strategy sections 2.1-2.2 and A15.
evidence: batch-b-truth-tests-v4.py full run: 6 failed, 43 passed, 3 subtests passed; BatchBReceiptContract enumerated 86 missing provenance items
blocking_findings.required_remediation: Obtain provider-exported, immutable event records for each active role; publish additive superseding receipts that bind exact prompt/context, distinct session and ancestry, fork_turns=none/raw isolation proof, start/end and final-response events, output bytes, and the committing revision. Rerun the receipt gate from the resulting immutable head.
blocking_findings.remediation_owner: orchestrator with the respective freshly isolated role providers

blocking_findings.title: Independent review is stale for the active browser evidence
blocking_findings.detail: batch-b-adversarial-review.json and its receipt are bound to role base 9455c2e, before browser-v3 was committed at 917fac54. The reviewer receipt has no input hash for batch-b-browser-audit-v3.json. The v4 fresh-review gate fails both active-browser-v3-hash-not-reviewed and audited-head-predates-active-browser-v3. Consequently the v3 browser disposition cannot be independently accepted, regardless of its local hash binding.
blocking_findings.required_remediation: Dispatch a new provider-attested, fresh-context adversarial reviewer after all selected bytes are committed. Require it to hash browser-v3, review a descendant head containing those bytes, rederive the B4 dispositions and findings, and publish an additive review and receipt; do not edit the prior review.
blocking_findings.remediation_owner: orchestrator and a newly isolated adversarial-reviewer

blocking_findings.title: Acceptance lifecycle is absent and must not be replayed or inferred
blocking_findings.detail: candidate-cohort-manifest-batch-b.json, product-owner-acceptance-batch-b.json, and accepted-cohort-manifest-batch-b.json are absent. The v4 suite fails the required existence and exact-byte/chronology contracts. No owner identity, approval event/message ID, thread, approval-message hash, or later-than-review approval event exists to evaluate for replay. The existing blocked review correctly authorizes no candidate or acceptance.
evidence: batch-b-truth-tests-v4.py full run: BatchBAcceptanceContract has three failing tests
blocking_findings.required_remediation: Only after authentic receipts, B4 evidence, and a fresh zero-blocker review are green, have the authorized product owner create a non-consumable exact-hash candidate, a resolved human approval event later than that review, and then a separate accepted manifest. Bind revocation/supersession state and reject reused approval identifiers or hashes.
blocking_findings.remediation_owner: authorized product owner, coordinated by the orchestrator

blocking_findings.title: Village Guardian terminal completion is not route/API complete
blocking_findings.detail: The browser-v3 audit records GET 200 and observed start, active, and terminal UI states, but both terminal POSTs to /api/v1/games/village-guardian/complete returned 400. The response reports required gameType, difficulty, score, duration, victory, idempotencyKey, and clientTimestamp as absent and xpEarned as unrecognized. This does not invalidate the bounded route/UI observation, but it prevents treating the terminal flow as successful completion, persistence, or idempotent progress behavior.
blocking_findings.required_remediation: Keep the route/UI and completion API claims separate. The owning application/API role must validate the completion payload contract and then obtain a fresh bounded browser/API observation with a valid idempotency key and timestamp before any end-to-end completion or persistence claim is made.

nonblocking_findings.title: Kimi WebBridge evidence states appropriate privacy and synthetic-input limitations, but these remain uncorroborated operational assertions
nonblocking_findings.detail: The audit limits use to Kimi WebBridge, reports one role-owned tab, no student-data records, no unrelated tabs, no published browser artifacts, and successful close_session for one tab. It also records isTrusted=false DOM events, a hidden tab, scheduler replacement limited to requestAnimationFrame, and no screenshots. These disclosures appropriately prevent claims of trusted native input, normal background-tab timing, screenshots, or student-data inspection; absent provider/session provenance means the assertions cannot establish an authenticated privacy or closure record.
nonblocking_findings.required_remediation: Retain the stated limitations and bind WebBridge session creation, tab inventory, network capture stop, and session closure to provider-exported evidence in a fresh receipt. Do not publish identifiable browser artifacts without an explicit privacy basis.

nonblocking_findings.title: Revision and path confinement are structurally preserved for the two additive v4 outputs
nonblocking_findings.detail: Commit d4e3fb5e adds only batch-b-truth-tests-v4.py and role-receipts/truth-test-author-batch-b-v4.json; its parent 917fac54 adds only browser-v3 audit and receipt. The immutable baseline is an ancestor and no committed Batch B artifact is modified in place in this two-commit remediation sequence. This is structural Git evidence only and does not cure the provenance failure.
nonblocking_findings.required_remediation: Preserve additive supersession and require the future review and lifecycle artifacts to bind their exact committed revision and input/output hashes.

test_strategy_violations: Required provider-authenticated fresh-context, fork_turns=none, event, final-response, and commit provenance is unavailable for active roles.
The active browser-v3 audit has not received a fresh independent review at a descendant exact-byte head.
The mandatory candidate-to-human-approval-to-accepted lifecycle has not been created and must not be inferred.
live_contract_violations: Village Guardian completion POST returned HTTP 400, so terminal UI observation is not successful completion API behavior.
WebBridge input was synthetic (isTrusted=false) and the hidden-tab terminal transition used a disclosed requestAnimationFrame adapter; no trusted-input or native-timing claim is supported.
route_parity_violations: Village Guardian route GET was observed as 200, while terminal completion POST was observed as 400; persistence/completion parity is unproved.
Archer's Revenge and Storm the Castle Tower have bounded exact-route 404 observations at browser-v3's role revision; these are non-runnable dispositions, not historical or source-wide conclusions.
